CausalChain: Hepatic circadian oscillations -> cyclic activation of PPARβ/δ -> enhanced synthesis of PC (18:0/18:1) and exosomal miRNA packaging -> exosome release into circulation -> uptake by muscle cells -> miRNA-induced epigenetic upregulation of PPARα -> increased muscle fatty acid oxidation -> improved systemic lipid metabolism
Hypothesis: Circadian-driven hepatic PPARβ/δ activation promotes the release of exosomes containing specific miRNAs and PC (18:0/18:1), which in turn induce epigenetic upregulation of muscle PPARα, thereby enhancing fatty acid oxidation and offering protection against metabolic disorders.
Abstract: We propose that the circadian regulation of hepatic PPARβ/δ activity not only drives the production of specific lipid mediators such as phosphatidylcholine (PC 18:0/18:1) but also facilitates the packaging of muscle-targeted microRNAs (miRNAs) within exosomes. These exosomes, released in a time‐dependent manner, may induce epigenetic modifications in skeletal muscle cells that elevate PPARα expression and enhance fatty acid oxidation. This liver-to-muscle communication axis could represent a novel endocrine mechanism by which the liver synchronizes systemic lipid homeostasis and energy utilization, protecting against diet-induced metabolic syndrome and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis.
